newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices end higher despite U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices end higher despite U.S. data.

text.p: Danish bond prices ended Tuesday well up, despite slightly stronger than expected U.S. industrial indicators.
"It has been a really positive day and the U.S. data could not damp sentiment," a dealer said.
"The numbers were much as expected and are not likely to cause much upset in the United States," he added.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.24 point from Monday's close to 106.04 in turnover of 2.5 billion crowns while its December future rose 0.06 point to 104.82, with 703 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was unchanged at 83.50.
The crown firmed to 3.8482 per mark from its earlier 3.8506.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 95 basis points.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of one billion crowns worth of a broad range of bonds. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
